boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all three frozen records in the Goldsboro Expedition. Preserve per-engagement dates: Kinston December 14, White Hall December 16 and Goldsborough Bridge December 17, 1862. Skirmishes on other days (Southwest Creek, Mount Olive, Thompson's Bridge) are not added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names Foster's 1st Division and Clingman's Brigade; the live field reads zero. Smith says Clingman had three regiments near the bridges and that the Union force was certainly over 15,000.
claims.rationale: Smith's estimate of Foster's force is an opponent's estimate and differs from Foster's own expedition total; no matched population. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Foster reports the railroad bridge burned and a Confederate advance on his rear guard repulsed as a disastrous failure; Smith says his brigades drove the Federals back from their position on the railroad line and saved the county bridge, and that the burned superstructure could be replaced at once.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The commanders frame the significance differently; the frozen label is retained. Both reports agree the railroad bridge burned; they conflict over the Confederate advance that followed. Neither account is adopted.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Foster's reports and G. W. Smith's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XVIII, are two further families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
